key_insight: The paper argues that full-duplex spoken language models fail mainly because speech and semantic processing interfere with each other. By separating acoustic and semantic pathways and enforcing semantic coherence, the model can sound more natural and stay more intelligible.
problem_solved: It addresses modality interference in full-duplex SLMs, where overlapping acoustic and language signals degrade knowledge retention, semantic consistency, and overall conversational quality.
method: Hierarchical acoustic-semantic modeling to disentangle low-level speech cues from high-level meaning.
Modality separation mechanisms to reduce interference between acoustic and semantic representations.
Semantic coherence objectives to preserve natural, context-consistent responses in full-duplex interaction.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this provides a clearer path to building speech models that respond smoothly in real time without losing semantic quality. It is especially relevant for developing more natural voice assistants, conversational agents, and spoken dialogue systems.
visual_elements: Before-and-after pipeline diagram showing modality interference vs. separated acoustic-semantic streams
Hierarchical model architecture graphic with acoustic and semantic layers
Comparison chart of naturalness, coherence, and intelligibility improvements
Icon set for speech waveform, text meaning, and full-duplex conversation
paper_title: Hierarchical Acoustic-Semantic Modeling: Modality Separation and Semantic Coherence for Full-Duplex SLMs
paper_authors: Zhenyu Liu, Yunxin Li, Xuanyu Zhang, Qixun Teng, Shenyuan Jiang
